# Permissions

Keelson only reads, on every provider. Each provider's section lists the data a scan reads and what grants it:
a token permission on Cloudflare, a team role on Vercel, IAM actions on AWS.

## Cloudflare

The simplest token is Cloudflare's **Read all resources** template, which covers almost everything below.
Two sources need more:

- **Account API tokens** need *Account API Tokens Read*, which the template doesn't include.
- **Logpush jobs** can only be listed with a write permission, so Keelson doesn't list them; it reads Logpush health from GraphQL analytics instead.

A source the token can't read shows up under **Scans → Data coverage** with the permission it needs, and the checks that depend on it are
skipped rather than passed. The setup screen tests a token against each source before you connect it.

| Source | Permission | Checks that read it |

These sources aren't Cloudflare API reads and need no permission:

- Public DNS lookups
- Takeover probes

## Vercel

Vercel access tokens can't be limited to reading: a token can do whatever its user's role allows on each team it reaches.
Keelson only ever sends GET requests to Vercel (`test/vercel.test.ts` fails on anything else), and never asks for environment
variable values. A token created by a member with the **Viewer** role reads almost everything below; environment variable names,
the firewall configuration, drains and webhooks need a role that can see them. Create the token under **Account Settings → Tokens**,
scoped to the team you want to scan (or Full Account for every team), with an expiration date.

| Source | Who can read it | Checks that read it |
|---|---|---|
| Team settings | Any team role (Viewer or higher) | VID-001, VID-008, VDP-007, VEN-006 |
| Team members and invitations | Any team role (Viewer or higher) | VID-002, VID-003, VID-004 |
| Your access tokens | A Full Account token (a token scoped to one team can't list tokens) | VID-005, VID-006, VID-007 |
| Projects | Any team role (Viewer or higher) | VDP-001, VDP-002, VDP-003, VDP-004, VDP-005, VDP-006, VDP-008, VEN-008, VFW-002, VPL-001, VPL-002, VPL-003, VPL-004, VPL-006, VPL-005, XP-003 |
| Environment variable names and types | Developer, Member or Owner | VDP-008, VEN-001, VEN-002, VEN-003, VEN-004, VEN-005, VEN-007 |
| Project domains | Any team role (Viewer or higher) | VDP-002, VFW-002, VDM-002, XP-003 |
| Firewall configuration | Developer, Member, Security or Owner | VFW-001, VFW-002, VFW-003, VFW-004, VFW-005, VFW-006, VFW-007 |
| Domains | Any team role (Viewer or higher) | VDM-001 |
| Custom certificates | Any team role (Viewer or higher) | VDM-003 |
| Drains | Member or Owner | VMN-001, VMN-002, VMN-003, VMN-004 |
| Webhooks | Member or Owner | VMN-003 |
| Installed integrations | Any team role (Viewer or higher) | VID-009 |
| Shared environment variable names and types | Developer, Member or Owner | Supporting data for other checks |

## AWS

An access key belongs to one AWS account, so each account needs its own. In each account, create an IAM user for Keelson,
attach AWS's managed **SecurityAudit** policy, and create an access key under **IAM → Users → the user → Security credentials**.
SecurityAudit reads configuration only: it can't change anything, and it can't read the objects in your buckets or the rows in your
databases. Temporary keys (the ones that start with ASIA) aren't accepted, because they expire within hours.

Keelson signs every request itself and only ever sends GET requests to AWS (`test/aws.test.ts` fails on anything else). Services
that can only be read with POST requests, such as CloudTrail, KMS and Config, aren't read yet. It never stores a policy document, a
Lambda environment variable or an instance's start-up script (the script is scanned for credentials in memory, and only the kind found
is kept), and keeps only the last four characters of an access key ID. To recognise DNS records that point at AWS addresses it also
reads AWS's public address-range file, without the access key.

Regional sources are read in every region enabled for the account. A region that refuses the access key (a service control policy,
for example) is skipped and shown as not readable on the Regions page: nothing there is checked or counted as passing.

| Source | IAM actions | Checks that read it |
|---|---|---|
| Account identity | `sts:GetCallerIdentity` | Supporting data for other checks |
| IAM account summary (root user) | `iam:GetAccountSummary` | AID-001, AID-002 |
| IAM password policy | `iam:GetAccountPasswordPolicy` | AID-007 |
| IAM users, their access keys and MFA devices | `iam:ListUsers`, `iam:ListAccessKeys`, `iam:GetAccessKeyLastUsed`, `iam:ListMFADevices`, `iam:GetLoginProfile` | AID-003, AID-004, AID-005, AID-006, AID-007, AID-008 |
| IAM roles, groups and policies | `iam:GetAccountAuthorizationDetails` | AID-008, AID-009, AID-010, AID-011, AEC-007 |
| S3 Block Public Access for the account | `s3:GetAccountPublicAccessBlock` | AS3-001, AS3-002, AS3-003 |
| S3 buckets | `s3:ListAllMyBuckets`, `s3:GetBucketLocation` | AS3-001, AS3-002, AS3-003, ADN-001 |
| S3 bucket access settings | `s3:GetBucketPublicAccessBlock`, `s3:GetBucketPolicyStatus`, `s3:GetBucketAcl` | AS3-002, AS3-003 |
| Enabled regions | `ec2:DescribeRegions` | Supporting data for other checks |
| Security groups (every enabled region) | `ec2:DescribeSecurityGroups` | ANW-001, ANW-002, ANW-003, AEC-007, ADB-001, XP-006 |
| Network interfaces and Elastic IPs (every enabled region) | `ec2:DescribeNetworkInterfaces`, `ec2:DescribeAddresses` | ANW-001, ANW-002, ANW-003, ADN-002, ADN-003, XP-006 |
| EC2 instances (every enabled region) | `ec2:DescribeInstances` | AEC-001, AEC-002, AEC-007, AEC-008, AMO-001, AMO-002 |
| EBS encryption, public snapshots and public images (every enabled region) | `ec2:GetEbsEncryptionByDefault`, `ec2:DescribeSnapshots`, `ec2:DescribeImages` | AEC-002, AEC-003, AEC-004 |
| VPCs and flow logs (every enabled region) | `ec2:DescribeVpcs`, `ec2:DescribeFlowLogs` | AMO-002 |
| RDS databases (every enabled region) | `rds:DescribeDBInstances` | ADB-001, ADB-002, ADB-003, AMO-001, AMO-002 |
| Load balancers and listeners (every enabled region) | `elasticloadbalancing:DescribeLoadBalancers`, `elasticloadbalancing:DescribeListeners`, `elasticloadbalancing:DescribeLoadBalancerAttributes` | AED-005, AED-006, ADN-001, AMO-001, AMO-002, AMO-003, XP-006 |
| Lambda functions and function URLs (every enabled region) | `lambda:ListFunctions`, `lambda:ListFunctionUrlConfigs` | AEC-005, AEC-006, AMO-001 |
| Instance start-up scripts (scanned for credentials, never stored) (every enabled region) | `ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute` | AEC-008 |
| API Gateway custom domain names (every enabled region) | `apigateway:GET` | Supporting data for other checks |
| GuardDuty detectors (every enabled region) | `guardduty:ListDetectors`, `guardduty:GetDetector` | AMO-001 |
| CloudFront distributions | `cloudfront:ListDistributions` | AED-001, AED-002, AED-003, AED-004, ADN-001 |
| Route 53 hosted zones and records | `route53:ListHostedZones`, `route53:ListResourceRecordSets` | ADN-001, ADN-002, ADN-003, XP-005 |
| AWS's published address ranges (ip-ranges.amazonaws.com) | `None: a public file`, `read without the access key` | ADN-003 |
